title: Configuring the ZCC Terraform provider: OneAPI credentials, environment variables and defaults

prose.text: The provider's own arguments, their types and descriptions are generated: run `node scripts/kb.mjs surface provider:zcc`. This subject holds how they are resolved and what the code does that the schema does not show.

prose.label: OneAPI only.
prose.text: {{oneapi-only-docs}} {{gov-clouds-unsupported}} The SDK's environment switch can still put it in legacy mode: [[zcc.sdk-go.legacy-routing:zcc-provider-oneapi-only]].

prose.label: Credentials.
prose.text: {{env-fallback}} {{auth-combination}} {{cloud-optional}} {{sdk-env-key-preferred}} The documentation says the secret and the private key conflict, but the code does not enforce it {{divergence:secret-key-conflict}}.

prose.label: Retries and timeouts.
prose.text: {{code-defaults}} The documented defaults are different {{divergence:retry-timeout-defaults}}. How the SDK applies these options and the proxy is in [[shared.sdk-go.request-handling:providers-append-proxy-after-rebuilds]], and which SDK release each provider build carries is [[shared.sdk-go.retries:provider-sdk-pins]].

checks.do: Whether the tenant is on Zidentity and a OneAPI cloud, since the provider has no legacy ZCC login and the government clouds are not supported.

Whether both a client secret and a private key are set, in configuration or the environment, and which one is in `ZSCALER_PRIVATE_KEY`, since nothing warns about the combination and a key in the environment wins.
Whether a slow failure came from the code's retry budget of 100 and 240-second timeout rather than the documented 5 and no limit.

oneapi-only-docs.statement: The provider documentation says it authenticates only through OneAPI OAuth2 via Zidentity, offers no legacy path (`zcc_client_id`, `zcc_client_secret` and `zcc_cloud` are not supported), and that tenants must be migrated to Zidentity before the provider can manage them.

quotes: The ZCC Terraform Provider authenticates exclusively via [OneAPI](https://help.zscaler.com/oneapi/understanding-oneapi) OAuth2 authentication through [Zidentity](https://help.zscaler.com/zidentity/what-zidentity).
This provider does **not** offer a legacy authentication path — the legacy ZCC V2 API client (`zcc_client_id` / `zcc_client_secret` / `zcc_cloud`) is not supported.
Tenants must be migrated to [Zidentity](https://help.zscaler.com/zidentity/what-zidentity) before they can be managed through this provider.

gov-clouds-unsupported.statement: The documentation says OneAPI and Zidentity are not currently supported for the `zscalergov` and `zscalerten` clouds.

quotes: Notice that OneAPI and Zidentity are not currently supported for the following clouds: `zscalergov` and `zscalerten`.

env-fallback.statement: Each credential and connection argument left unset in the provider block is read from an environment variable: `ZSCALER_CLIENT_ID`, `ZSCALER_CLIENT_SECRET`, `ZSCALER_PRIVATE_KEY`, `ZSCALER_VANITY_DOMAIN`, `ZSCALER_CLOUD` and `ZSCALER_HTTP_PROXY`.

auth-combination.statement: The client is built only from a client ID and a vanity domain together with either a client secret or a private key; otherwise configuration fails with 'invalid authentication configuration: missing required parameters'. The cloud is passed only when set.

quotes: invalid authentication configuration: missing required parameters (client_id, client_secret or private_key, vanity_domain)

cloud-optional.statement: The documentation says `zscaler_cloud` is optional and needed only when authenticating to other environments such as `beta`.

quotes: The `zscaler_cloud` is optional and only required when authenticating to other environments i.e `beta`

code-defaults.statement: When unset, the code uses 100 retries, a 240-second request timeout, and a minimum and maximum retry wait of 2 and 10 seconds. An explicit 0 is replaced the same way, so `request_timeout = 0` becomes 240 seconds and `max_retries = 0` becomes 100.
code-defaults.conditions: Added the explicit-0 case: `getIntValue` passes a set 0 through, then `applyDefaults` overwrites any 0.

sdk-env-key-preferred.statement: The SDK loads `ZSCALER_PRIVATE_KEY` (and `~/.zscaler/zscaler.yaml`) into its own configuration and authenticates with a JWT whenever a private key is present, so a key in the environment wins even when the provider took the secret branch. In that case a file path in the variable is used as the key text, because the provider's `WithPrivateKey`, which reads a path, is not called.
sdk-env-key-preferred.conditions: envconfig v1.4.0 falls back to the unprefixed tag name; traced, not run.

quotes: // If private key is provided, use JWT-based authentication.
// WithPrivateKey sets private key, privateKey can be the raw key value or a path to the pem file.

secret-key-conflict.summary: Whether `client_secret` and `private_key` may both be set: the documentation says they conflict, while the code has no conflict check; the provider passes the secret when both are present, but the SDK still prefers a key it reads from the environment.

positions.says: The argument reference says `client_secret` conflicts with `private_key`.

The client builder tests the secret combination first and passes only the secret to the SDK when both are set, without an error; the SDK still authenticates with a key it reads from the environment itself (sdk-env-key-preferred).

secret-key-conflict.impact: A private key set only in the provider block is silently unused when `ZSCALER_CLIENT_SECRET` is also in the environment. In reverse, a secret set in the provider block is ignored when `ZSCALER_PRIVATE_KEY` is in the environment, because the SDK authenticates with that key, and a key path there is used raw rather than read from the file. Both matter when rotating between secret and key authentication.

resolution.note: The code decides what the provider does; the documentation states an intent the schema does not enforce.

retry-timeout-defaults.summary: The defaults for `max_retries` and `request_timeout`: the documentation says 5 retries and a timeout of 0 (no limit, at most 300), while the code uses 100 retries and 240 seconds.

positions.says: The argument reference gives a `max_retries` default of 5 and a `request_timeout` default of 0, meaning no limit, with a maximum of 300.

quotes: Maximum number of retries to attempt before returning an error, the default is `5`.
the default is `0` (means no limit is set). The maximum value can be `300`.

positions.says: The configure code defaults the retry count to 100 and the request timeout to 240 seconds.

retry-timeout-defaults.impact: An apply against a rate-limited or unreachable API can keep retrying far longer than the documentation suggests. Set both arguments explicitly, and non-zero, when the bound matters: an explicit `request_timeout = 0`, documented as no limit, becomes 240 seconds, and `max_retries = 0` becomes 100 (code-defaults).
